subject: Edge fabric topology and ephemeral store coordination
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Tom Baker <tbaker@acmehealth.com>, opsinfra@acmehealth.com
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Edge fabric topology and ephemeral store coordination

Tom / Acme infra team —

Thanks for the sync today. As promised I'm capturing the core decisions and open questions for the on‑prem cluster we’ll be delivering in Q4. This will be the private Redwood control plane + customer‑managed data plane (VPC/on‑prem) pattern we discussed. Key asks below so we can finalize the runbook and sizing workbook I attached.

Quick summary / constraints:
- Expected steady token throughput: ~35 qps peak (3k tokens/min sustained) for the inference service; burst to ~120 qps during batch scoring windows.
- Max model context length: 8k; average session length today ~1.2k tokens.
- Regional requirements: primary site is your NJ colo, DR in our AWS us‑east region.
- Security: customer VPC with MD VPN to Redwood; egress must go through your perimeter NAT (no direct internet from worker nodes).

Cluster requirements (draft):
- Control plane: two control plane nodes (HA) in a management VLAN; we recommend the customer run these in a dedicated management rack or VM cluster.
- Worker pools: three node pools
  * inference-hot: 4 x A5000-equivalent (or your nv4) nodes, local NVMe for model KV cache (recommend 2–4 TB NVMe per node)
  * inference-cold: 8 x T4-equivalent for batch & fallback (no local NVMe required; use blockstore PVCs)
  * infra: 3 x general purpose (monitoring / logging / ingress)
- Node labeling / taints: inference nodes will be tainted inference=true:NoSchedule; workloads use tolerations.

Storage & PVC strategy:
- Persistent model artifacts (immutable): stored on blockstore (encrypted). PVC class: fast-block (io1) with encryption-at-rest; lifecycle via retain-on-delete for artifacts.
- Ephemeral KV cache: use hostPath -> local NVMe with a CSI-localpv that mounts to /var/lib/redwood-kv; enforce eviction policy on start.
- Prometheus / metrics: 100GB PVC on medium-tier blockstore; retain 30 days.

Networking & egress rules:
- Nodes must not have public IPs. Egress SNAT via your perimeter NAT pool; Redwood control plane will reach agent over TCP 443 outbound only.
- Ports: 10250 (kubelet) restricted to management IPs; 9000–9100 for model debug only over management network; control plane components over 443.
- BGP or static routes supported — please confirm which you prefer for cross‑site traffic.

Open questions (please answer inline):
1) Confirm available local NVMe per inference rack (size + per-shelf quantity).
2) Do you have a preferred blockstore provider/version (Ceph/OE/NetApp)? Any max IOPS constraints?
3) Will we be permitted to run NAT egress for Redwood agents to our control plane (outbound only)?
4) Any compliance constraints for logging retention beyond 30 days?

Next steps:
- Please review and reply with the three answers above. We'll update the attached pv‑sizing workbook and iterate the topology graphic before the PoC kickoff.

Attachments: edge-topology-v1.png (diagram), pv-sizing-acme.xlsx (sizing workbook), network-checklist-acme.pdf (security checklist)

Thanks —
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

From: Tom Baker <tbaker@acmehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, opsinfra@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-10-11T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Edge fabric topology and ephemeral store coordination

Naomi — thanks for the thorough note. A few quick answers while we loop in facilities for exact NVMe counts: 

1) NVMe per inference rack: current shelves have 4 x 3.2TB NVMe per host available for allocation; we can provision up to 6TB if needed but that's vendor lead time. For PoC we can do 3.2TB per node.
2) Blockstore: we're standardized on Ceph (Pacific) for this colo. We can provide a fast RBD class with 10k IOPS sustained per volume; ops will confirm headroom.
3) Egress/NAT: yes, outbound to Redwood control plane is allowed. We need a CA-signed cert for the agent and we will only allow 443 outbound to Greenwood endpoints.
4) Logging retention: healthcare regs require 1 year for audit logs; we can keep metrics for 90 days. We need to discuss scrubbed PII handling on traces.

Two additional items:
- Can Redwood agent support a proxy for outbound control-plane traffic? Our environment forces forced‑proxying for some racks.
- For the batch fallback path, we'd prefer to limit network egress during scheduled nightly job windows — can Redwood schedule model downloads outside of that window?

I'll have ops attach the Ceph pool config and a CSV with actual host inventory by EOD.

—Tom
Tom Baker
Director, Infrastructure — Acme Health
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Tom Baker <tbaker@acmehealth.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Edge fabric topology and ephemeral store coordination

Thanks Tom — helpful. A few technical clarifications from our runtime/ops perspective: 

- NVMe sizing: 3.2TB per inference node is workable for PoC. We typically size KV cache so that hot prefixes stay resident — for your traffic profile I'd recommend reserving 1.2–1.8TB of NVMe for the KV cache and leave ~1TB for local model shards and temp files. We'll ship a startup script that enforces a soft quota.

- Ceph: Pacific RBD is fine. We will request a provisioner name for the fast-block StorageClass (we'll use longhorn as fallback if RBD rules become complex during PoC). Please send the RBD secret and pool name to our secure upload link.

- Agent egress: our agent supports HTTPS outbound and also supports connecting via an HTTP CONNECT proxy. We'll need an allowlist IP range for the proxy and certificate thumbprint. If the proxy terminates TLS, please confirm whether mutual TLS will still be required.

- Nightly downloads: yes, we can schedule model pulls (and heavy remote checkpoints) to run in a configured maintenance window. We'll expose that as a deploy-time flag and can throttle concurrency to avoid saturating your Ceph pool.

Operational asks for runbook: 
- Health probes: kube liveness/readiness for inference pods should hit /healthz and verify KV cache mount + local disk free > 12%.
- Eviction policy: prefer soft eviction with pod cordon and graceful shutdown to drain model state to blockstore (where applicable).
- Canary: we'll do a 10% canary on the inference-hot pool for the first rollout and monitor latency and error-rate for 2 hours before ramp.

I'll update the workbook with the NVMe values you provided and the Ceph pool once we get it. Attaching a short checklist (network-checklist-acme.pdf) with the proxy options filled in — see page 2.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Tom Baker <tbaker@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Edge fabric topology and ephemeral store coordination

All — quick confirmation from my side: PoC plan accepted with the following constraints we captured during the call: 
- PoC topology: 3 inference-hot nodes (reduce from 4) to start, 3 inference-cold nodes; scale to target footprint after load testing.
- Use Ceph Pacific fast-block; set default PVC IOPS limit at 10k; Redwood to throttle concurrent downloads to 4 streams per rack.
- Agent via HTTP CONNECT proxy supported; Tom to provide proxy IPs and thumbprint.
- Logging retention: we will keep audit logs for 12 months and metrics for 90 days; any PII in traces will be scrubbed before storage.

I will schedule a short technical kickoff tomorrow 09:00 ET to finalize the startup scripts and attach the Ceph secret exchange instructions to Jira INF-4521. Naomi/Dev — please confirm the kickoff invite time works for you.

Thanks —
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Deployment Engineering, Redwood Inference
